cmp.eli5: The exact price at which a stock was last bought or sold on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) or Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
cmp.formula: Last recorded match price between buyer bid and seller ask.
cmp.whyItMatters: CMP tells you what you need to pay right now to own 1 share of the company.

benchmarks.green: Reasonable entry price when backed by growing revenues and low debt.
benchmarks.red: CMP inflated far beyond the company's real underlying earnings power.

cmp.example: If Reliance trades at ₹1,202.00 on the NSE feed, that ₹1,202.00 is its CMP.

peRatio.eli5: How many rupees investors are willing to pay for every ₹1 of annual profit earned by the company.
peRatio.formula: Current Market Price (CMP) ÷ Earnings Per Share (EPS Trailing TTM)
peRatio.whyItMatters: It is the primary measuring tape of whether a stock is cheap or expensive compared to peers.

benchmarks.green: 15x – 28x is standard for stable Indian blue-chip companies.
benchmarks.red: > 60x without fast profit growth indicates overvaluation or bubble risk.

peRatio.example: If a company earns ₹50 EPS and trades at ₹1,000 CMP, its P/E is 20x.

industryPe.eli5: The average Price-to-Earnings multiple across all listed peer companies in the same industry.
industryPe.formula: Average P/E of all listed companies in the specific industry sector.
industryPe.whyItMatters: Comparing a stock's P/E to its Industry P/E reveals if it enjoys a quality premium or trades at a discount.

benchmarks.green: Trading below or inline with Industry P/E with superior margins.
benchmarks.red: Trading at 3x the Industry P/E without higher profit compounding.

industryPe.example: If Indian IT sector average P/E is 27x and Infosys trades at 25x, Infosys is trading at a sector discount.

pbRatio.eli5: Compares current stock price against the net tangible liquidation value of the balance sheet.
pbRatio.formula: Current Market Price (CMP) ÷ Book Value Per Share (BVPS)
pbRatio.whyItMatters: Essential for valuing banks, NBFCs, and asset-heavy industries like steel and energy.

benchmarks.green: Banks: 1.5x – 2.8x is healthy. Manufacturing: < 3x.
benchmarks.red: Excessive P/B (> 8x) in capital-intensive manufacturing signals speculative risk.

pbRatio.example: A P/B of 2.0x means you pay ₹2 in the market for every ₹1 of net accounting assets.

roe.eli5: Measures how efficiently management turns shareholders' equity into net profit.
roe.whyItMatters: High ROE proves management can generate strong profits without constant equity dilution.

benchmarks.green: ROE > 18% is great in India; > 25% is world-class (e.g. TCS).
benchmarks.red: ROE < 10% means returns lag corporate borrowing rates or safe fixed deposits.

roe.example: If a company has ₹1,000 Cr net worth and makes ₹250 Cr net profit, ROE is 25%.

roce.eli5: The gold-standard test of capital efficiency: how much operating profit is generated from ALL capital (Equity + Debt).
roce.formula: (Operating Profit EBIT ÷ Capital Employed [Total Assets - Current Liabilities]) × 100
roce.whyItMatters: Unlike ROE (which can be masked by taking loans), ROCE shows if debt is generating real profits.

benchmarks.green: ROCE > 20% indicates a strong economic moat and sustainable pricing power.
benchmarks.red: ROCE < 12% means returns barely cover the cost of debt.

roce.example: TCS generates ~60% ROCE, meaning every ₹100 of capital employed yields ~₹60 in annual EBIT.

debtToEquity.eli5: Shows how heavily the company relies on borrowed loans compared to shareholders' equity.
debtToEquity.whyItMatters: High debt creates high interest obligations during economic slowdowns or rising rate cycles.

benchmarks.green: D/E < 0.5x is conservative and very safe.
benchmarks.red: D/E > 1.5x in non-banking companies poses severe solvency danger.

debtToEquity.example: A D/E of 0.1x means the company has only ₹10 of debt for every ₹100 of net worth.

marketCap.eli5: The total rupee value of all the company's shares combined.
marketCap.formula: Current Market Price (CMP) × Total Number of Issued Shares
marketCap.whyItMatters: Classifies Indian stocks into Large Cap (> ₹20,000 Cr), Mid Cap (₹5,000 - ₹20,000 Cr), and Small Cap (< ₹5,000 Cr).

benchmarks.green: Large caps offer institutional stability and high liquidity.
benchmarks.red: Micro-caps (< ₹500 Cr) carry illiquidity and sharp swing risks.

marketCap.example: Reliance Industries has an M-Cap of ~₹18 Lakh Crore, making it India's largest enterprise.

dividendYield.eli5: The annual cash payout distributed directly to shareholder bank accounts as a percentage of share price.
dividendYield.formula: (Annual Dividend Per Share ÷ Current Market Price) × 100
dividendYield.whyItMatters: Provides steady passive income even during sideways or bear market phases.

benchmarks.green: 2.0% – 4.5% is a healthy dividend yield for cash-generative Indian companies (e.g. ITC).
benchmarks.red: 0% in mature companies with no growth, or > 10% signaling dividend trap.

dividendYield.example: If ITC pays ₹14.50 dividend per share and trades at ₹462, the yield is ~3.15%.

netProfit.eli5: The bottom-line profit after paying all operating expenses, depreciation, interest, and taxes for the latest quarter.
netProfit.formula: Total Revenue minus Total Expenses (Operating, Interest, Tax)
netProfit.whyItMatters: Quarterly net profit directly drives market expectations and institutional buying interest.

benchmarks.green: Growing Net Profit with double-digit profit margins (> 15%).
benchmarks.red: Dipping into losses or declining profit margins YoY.

netProfit.example: TCS reports ~₹12,000 Cr net profit per quarter.

profitVariance.eli5: The percentage growth or decline in net profit compared to the same quarter last year (YoY) or prior quarter (QoQ).
profitVariance.formula: [(Current Qtr Profit - Previous Qtr Profit) ÷ Previous Qtr Profit] × 100
profitVariance.whyItMatters: Earnings acceleration or deceleration dictates whether the stock gets re-rated higher or lower.

benchmarks.green: Positive profit variance > 12% indicates robust earnings acceleration.
benchmarks.red: Negative profit variance indicates slowing demand or margin compression.

profitVariance.example: +18.5% YoY profit variance signals the company is expanding profits faster than inflation.

quarterlySales.eli5: The total top-line revenue collected from products sold or services delivered during the quarter.
quarterlySales.formula: Sum of all sales invoices and contract revenue realized in the quarter.
quarterlySales.whyItMatters: Revenue growth is the foundational engine of business expansion; profit cannot grow indefinitely without sales growth.

benchmarks.green: Steady 10% – 20% annualized revenue compounding.
benchmarks.red: Stagnant or declining sales indicating loss of market share.

quarterlySales.example: Reliance quarterly revenue exceeds ₹2.3 Lakh Crore across energy, retail, and digital.

salesVariance.eli5: The percentage expansion or contraction in total revenue compared to prior reporting period.
salesVariance.formula: [(Current Qtr Sales - Prior Qtr Sales) ÷ Prior Qtr Sales] × 100
salesVariance.whyItMatters: Tracks commercial market share gains and customer demand velocity.

benchmarks.green: > 10% YoY sales growth for large caps; > 20% for mid-caps.
benchmarks.red: Negative sales variance signaling softening demand.

salesVariance.example: +14.2% sales variance means business scale expanded by 14.2% YoY.

rsi.eli5: A momentum oscillator scaled 0 to 100 measuring the speed and size of recent price changes.
rsi.formula: 100 - [100 ÷ (1 + Average Gain ÷ Average Loss)] over 14 candles.
rsi.whyItMatters: Alerts you if buyers pushed the price too high (Overbought) or sellers panicked too hard (Oversold).

benchmarks.green: 45 – 65: Ideal trending momentum zone.
benchmarks.red: > 70: Overbought (pullback risk); < 30: Oversold (potential bounce).

rsi.example: An RSI of 58 confirms steady upward momentum without being overextended.

macdSignal.eli5: A trend-following momentum indicator displaying the distance between fast (12-period) and slow (26-period) EMAs.
macdSignal.formula: 12-period EMA minus 26-period EMA; triggered by 9-period Signal line.
macdSignal.whyItMatters: A Bullish Crossover (MACD crossing above signal line) signals the start of a fresh upward impulse.

benchmarks.green: Bullish Crossover above zero line indicates strong buyer control.
benchmarks.red: Bearish Crossover below zero line indicates intensifying downward pressure.

macdSignal.example: A fresh Bullish MACD crossover on the 15-minute chart triggers intraday long momentum.

investiqScore.eli5: A comprehensive 0 to 100 rating synthesized across 5 key pillars of financial and market strength.
investiqScore.formula: Fundamentals (35 pts) + Technicals (30 pts) + Volume/Perf (15 pts) + News Sentiment (10 pts) + Valuation (10 pts)
investiqScore.whyItMatters: Gives investors an instant, holistic view of whether a company is fundamentally sound, technically strong, and attractively valued.

benchmarks.green: Score >= 70 (Strong Outlook): High quality, positive momentum, sound balance sheet.
benchmarks.red: Score < 45 (Weaker / High Risk): Multiple headwinds across valuation, debt, or technicals.

investiqScore.example: A score of 78/100 signifies strong fundamentals with bullish technical alignment.

mlPrediction.eli5: A multi-horizon machine learning model trained on historical volatility, returns, ATR, VWAP gap, and volume.
mlPrediction.formula: Ensemble Random Forest classifier & regressor predicting price direction and range for 1d, 2d, 3d, or 1w horizons.
mlPrediction.whyItMatters: Provides algorithmic probability of price continuation vs reversal based on historical patterns.

benchmarks.green: Bullish model direction aligned with positive volume ratio and RSI momentum.
benchmarks.red: Bearish model direction warning of mean-reversion or breakdown risk.

mlPrediction.example: Predicted close of ₹1,215 with range ₹1,195 – ₹1,230 on a 1-day horizon.

candleOHLCV.eli5: A Japanese candlestick displaying Open, High, Low, Close, and Volume for a specific timeframe.
candleOHLCV.formula: Body shows Open to Close; wicks show High and Low; volume bar shows total traded shares.
candleOHLCV.whyItMatters: Shows the battle between bulls and bears during that specific trading interval.

benchmarks.green: Green candle: Close > Open (buyers won the interval).
benchmarks.red: Red candle: Close < Open (sellers pushed price down).

candleOHLCV.example: A 10-minute candle showing Open ₹3,450, High ₹3,465, Low ₹3,448, Close ₹3,462 with 250k volume.

intraday10m.eli5: A completed 10-minute chart bar accurately aggregated from two consecutive 5-minute exchange candles.
intraday10m.formula: Open of candle 1, Max High of both, Min Low of both, Close of candle 2, Summed Volume.
intraday10m.whyItMatters: Smooths out noisy 5-minute intraday fluctuations while preserving timely entry/exit signals.

benchmarks.green: Higher highs and higher lows on consecutive 10m candles indicate intraday trend continuation.
benchmarks.red: Bearish engulfing pattern on high volume signaling intraday reversal.

intraday10m.example: Aggregated from 09:15-09:20 and 09:20-09:25 candles to produce the 09:15-09:25 10m bar.

compositeRating.eli5: A head-to-head scorecard evaluating two companies across 10 critical financial and operational dimensions.
compositeRating.formula: Winner determined by comparing P/E, ROE, ROCE, D/E, Margins, Growth, Technicals, and Sentiment.
compositeRating.whyItMatters: Instantly settles stock debates by showing which company dominates the key fundamental and technical metrics.

benchmarks.green: Winning 7+ out of 10 categories demonstrates clear sector leadership.
benchmarks.red: Losing both valuation and efficiency categories flags underperformance.

compositeRating.example: In TCS vs INFY, TCS secures wins in ROCE (61% vs 31%) and Operating Margin (24.6% vs 20.8%).
